notes: Four adversarial rounds, the first three DISAGREE, each finding a real defect that was reproduced before being fixed. Round 1: the PR's own first commit turned a fail-closed path into a fail-open one -- Path.resolve preserves a Windows extended-length prefix, so a path genuinely inside the repo failed relative_to and was read as 'outside, not our business', allowing a claude-agent write into plugins/codex. Round 2: the same defect in two more spellings, //?/ and a UNC admin share, both confirmed to produce real writes at the aliased location rather than mere classifier confusion. Round 3, and the best of them: an unresolved '..' in a RELATIVE path, no Windows trick involved -- classify_path matches prefixes, so a codex apply_patch header naming plugins/codex/../../plugins/claude/evil.py was waved through as codex's own lane. That is codex's only realistic transport, and three rounds of absolute-path hardening had never touched that branch. Round 4 returned AGREE: the reviewer could not make any input reach another lane's real file, confirmed the earlier classes stay closed, and confirmed 2 of the 4 new tests discriminate against the pre-fix code while naming the other 2 as non-discriminating guards. Two non-blocking follow-ups it raised were then fixed in this PR rather than deferred: a bare '..' classified as 'shared' instead of failing closed, and a stale .git entry truncating a nested worktree path at the wrong depth. Throughout, the reviewer independently confirmed the CI enforcement of record is untouched by all of this: a git tree path can never carry a '..' component or a UNC prefix, so lws-lanes sees only clean final paths. The hook is a same-session nudge and the module docstring now says so, including that it never sees a write made through a shell.
